hero.h1: ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant in Bangalore
hero.intro: ARTAS iX is a robotic hair-restoration system designed to assist experts during selected stages of hair transplantation. At NeoSculpt6, ARTAS technology is considered only after a detailed hair-loss, scalp and donor-area assessment.

buttons.label: Book an ARTAS Hair Transplant Consultation

intro.h2: What Is ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration?
paragraphs: ARTAS iX uses robotic technology and a high-definition stereoscopic vision system to identify suitable hair follicular units from the scalp. The system can support experts during follicular-unit harvesting, recipient-site creation and implantation as part of a clinically planned hair-transplant procedure.

Treatment planning remains specialist led. The choice of technique depends on the pattern of hair loss, donor availability, scalp condition, hair characteristics and the result the patient hopes to achieve.

comparison.h2: How Is ARTAS Different From Traditional Hair Transplant Procedures?
comparison.introLine: Traditional hair restoration procedures include Follicular Unit Transplantation (FUT) and manual Follicular Unit Excision (FUE). The appropriate method depends on the individual assessment and treatment plan.

cards.title: Follicular Unit Transplantation (FUT)
cards.text: FUT involves removing a strip of scalp from the back of the head and separating the hair follicles from it for implantation into balding areas. Because it involves strip removal, FUT leaves a permanent linear scar, and some patients may experience scalp numbness, tingling, tightness or discomfort during recovery.

cards.title: Manual Follicular Unit Excision (FUE)
cards.text: Manual FUE uses handheld instruments to extract individual hair grafts. The procedure relies on the expert’s or technician’s hand-eye coordination and involves repetitive graft extraction during surgery.

cards.title: ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration
cards.text: ARTAS iX uses robotic technology to assist experts with precise and repetitive movements during follicular-unit harvesting. It is designed to identify suitable grafts, assist with extraction, create recipient sites and implant harvested follicles as part of the planned procedure.

process.h2: How Does the ARTAS iX Procedure Work?

steps.title: High-Definition Stereoscopic Vision
steps.text: The ARTAS iX high-definition stereoscopic vision system identifies grafts suitable for harvesting and provides detailed visualisation during the procedure.

steps.title: Precise Follicular-Unit Harvesting
steps.text: The ARTAS iX harvesting system helps the expert dissect and harvest grafts from the donor area. Robotic technology supports consistent repetitive movements throughout this stage of the procedure.

steps.title: Recipient-Site Creation
steps.text: After harvesting, the ARTAS iX system can create recipient sites according to the individual treatment plan, hairline design and graft-placement strategy.

steps.title: Site Making and Implantation
steps.text: ARTAS iX can support recipient-site making and implantation of harvested grafts. The treatment team plans every stage around the patient’s existing hair, donor area and restoration goal.

benefits.h2: What Are the Benefits of ARTAS iX?

cards.title: No Linear Scar
cards.text: ARTAS-assisted follicular-unit extraction does not use a strip-removal approach, so it does not create a linear donor scar.

cards.title: No Plugs, Stitches or Staples
cards.text: The procedure is designed around individual follicular units rather than the plug-graft approach used in older transplant methods. It does not involve strip closure with stitches or staples.

cards.title: Precise Graft Harvesting and Implantation
cards.text: Robotic technology supports detailed imaging, graft identification and repeatable procedural movements during the planned stages of treatment.

cards.title: Natural-Looking Hair-Restoration Planning
cards.text: Hairline design, graft placement and density goals are planned around the individual’s facial proportions, existing hair, donor availability and long-term expectations.

benefits.smallPrint: Individual results, recovery experience and visible growth vary between patients.

items: Men and women with androgenetic alopecia
Hair and donor characteristics suitable for the technology-assisted procedure
Hair-loss pattern, donor area and scalp condition assessed first
paragraphs: ARTAS iX may be considered for men and women with androgenetic alopecia where hair and donor characteristics are suitable for the technology-assisted procedure. Hair-loss pattern, donor area, scalp condition and hair characteristics are assessed before treatment is recommended.
The expert determines whether ARTAS-assisted treatment is appropriate after evaluating the patient’s hair loss and donor area.

expectations.h2: What Results Can You Expect From ARTAS iX?
paragraphs: Hair restoration develops gradually after treatment. Visible change is reviewed over time, with hair-transplant progress commonly assessed at different stages of the growth cycle. Actual growth, density, recovery and final appearance vary between patients.

items.q: What is ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration?
items.a: ARTAS iX is a robotic hair-restoration system designed to assist experts during selected stages of hair transplantation, including follicular-unit harvesting, recipient-site creation and implantation.

items.q: Is ARTAS different from FUT and manual FUE?
items.a: Yes. FUT removes a strip of scalp and leaves a linear scar, and manual FUE uses handheld instruments. ARTAS iX uses robotic technology to assist experts with precise and repetitive movements during harvesting.

items.q: Does ARTAS leave a linear scar?
items.a: ARTAS-assisted follicular-unit extraction does not use a strip-removal approach, so it does not create a linear donor scar.

hero.intro: Plan your hair, skin, aesthetic, body-contouring or fertility consultation journey with clear clinical guidance before you travel to Bangalore. The process begins with your concern and the information your doctor needs—not with a preset package.

intro.h2: Not Medical Tourism Packages. A Care Plan.
paragraphs: International care works best when the clinical pathway is understood before travel. NeoSculpt6 helps patients begin with a structured conversation, share the information relevant to their concern and understand what may need an in-person assessment. Recommendations are made around diagnosis, suitability, preparation and realistic treatment goals.

cards.title: Share the Context
cards.text: Tell us what you would like help with, your country of residence, preferred travel window and any previous treatment history. This helps the team route your enquiry appropriately.

cards.title: Share Relevant Records
cards.text: Depending on the concern, we may request reports, prescriptions, investigations, photographs or short videos. Hair enquiries may need scalp and donor-area photographs; other treatments have different information requirements.

cards.title: Speak With the Right Team
cards.text: A preliminary review or virtual consultation helps you understand the relevant clinical pathway, preparation, likely clinic visits and the next decision to make before travelling.

tabs.paragraph: For hair thinning, pattern hair loss and transplant enquiries, the pathway may include virtual review, donor assessment, scalp examination, graft planning where appropriate, treatment guidance and follow-up planning.
For acne scars, pigmentation, texture concerns, vitiligo, laser procedures and skin refinement, recommendations depend on diagnosis, skin type, treatment history and recovery requirements.
For anti-ageing and injectable-treatment enquiries, the consultation focuses on skin and facial assessment, treatment goals, appropriate options, safety considerations and realistic outcomes.
For surgical aesthetic enquiries, the in-person consultation focuses on anatomy, medical suitability, procedure options, recovery planning and what can realistically be achieved.

For localised body-shape, fat-reduction, skin-tightening or body-contouring concerns, the team assesses the treatment area, skin quality, anatomy, lifestyle factors and whether a surgical or non-surgical approach may be appropriate.
For fertility-related concerns, the team can explain the consultation pathway and the records or investigations that may be relevant before a treatment plan is considered.

journey.h2: The Plan Continues After You Arrive.

steps.title: Initial Enquiry
steps.text: Share your concern and preferred timeline.

steps.title: Records Review
steps.text: Provide the information requested for a preliminary review.

steps.title: Virtual Consultation
steps.text: Discuss the likely pathway, suitability questions and preparation.

steps.title: Visit Planning
steps.text: Plan appointments around the recommended consultation, treatment and early recovery period.

steps.title: In-Person Clinical Assessment
steps.text: The specialist confirms the clinical factors that cannot be assessed fully online.

steps.title: Treatment and Recovery
steps.text: If treatment is appropriate, you receive a personalised plan, aftercare instructions and recovery guidance.

steps.title: Follow-Up
steps.text: Where appropriate, the team explains the recommended remote review process after you return home.

travel.h2: What to Arrange Before You Travel.
paragraphs: Keep relevant reports, prescriptions and treatment history organised. Tell the team about medical conditions, allergies, medications and previous procedures so that the consultation can be planned safely.

The right length of stay depends on your treatment, number of required visits, procedure plan and early recovery review. Avoid tightly scheduled travel around consultations or procedures. Visa, travel and accommodation arrangements remain the responsibility of the patient and the relevant authorities.

On arrival, the appropriate specialist completes the in-person assessment, reviews the treatment goals and confirms whether the proposed plan remains suitable. You should understand the expected outcome, limitations, aftercare, alternatives and follow-up before deciding how to proceed.
